Image files, dimensions, and alt text

The src points to a file. Use JPEG for photos, PNG for lossless graphics or transparency, SVG for scalable diagrams, and WebP when it gives a smaller suitable file. Set width and height to reserve space at the correct aspect ratio. Describe what matters in alt. Use alt="" for decoration.

How to try it In index.html, replace the content between <body> and </body> with this example. Save the file and reload it in the browser.

<img src="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/docs/media/html/workshop-480.webp"
     alt="Diagram illustrating a client communicating with a server"
     width="480" height="270">

What to expect The diagram loads into a reserved 480-by-270 area.

Connect a figure to its visible caption

Use figure for self-contained material worth referring to as a unit. A figcaption gives readers visible context. The alt text still explains meaningful visual information to readers who cannot see the image.

How to try it In index.html, replace the content between <body> and </body> with this example. Save the file and reload it in the browser.

<figure>
  <img src="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/docs/media/html/workshop-480.webp"
       width="480" height="270"
       alt="Client and server connected over a network">
  <figcaption>Figure 1. The two sides of a web request.</figcaption>
</figure>

What to expect The caption appears directly below the diagram.

Choose a file based on the available space

Use width descriptors in srcset and tell the browser the intended layout width with sizes. It can pick a candidate using the layout width and display density. Use picture for a different crop, for example a square image on a narrow screen. Use loading="lazy" on images farther down the page.

How to try it In index.html, replace the content between <body> and </body> with this example. Save the file and reload it in the browser.

<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 500px)" srcset="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/docs/media/html/workshop-square.webp"
          width="480" height="480">
  <img src="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/docs/media/html/workshop-480.webp"
       srcset="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/docs/media/html/workshop-480.webp 480w, https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/docs/media/html/workshop-960.webp 960w"
       sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 480px"
       width="480" height="270" style="max-width:100%;height:auto"
       loading="lazy" alt="A diagram of a client and a server">
</picture>

What to expect Resize the preview and look at the requested file in DevTools.

Play audio and video or embed a page

The controls attribute adds a player. List available files with source and supply a video poster to show before playback. A track links to a WebVTT captions file. Give an iframe a descriptive title so its purpose is clear when a reader reaches it.

How to try it In index.html, replace the content between <body> and </body> with this example. Save the file and reload it in the browser.

<audio controls preload="none">
  <source src="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/media/lesson.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
</audio>
<video controls width="420" style="max-width:100%"
       poster="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/docs/media/html/workshop-480.webp">
  <source src="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/media/lesson.webm" type="video/webm">
  <track kind="captions" src="https://javascript-training.cloudninemm.com/media/lesson-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
</video>
<iframe title="Workshop location note"
        srcdoc="<p>Location: North Hall, Room 2.</p>"></iframe>

What to expect Try the audio and the video controls. Turn on English captions in the video player.

Hands-on exercise

Create a three-image gallery. Give each figure a caption and an alt attribute. Test one broken image path, then restore it. Add a video with controls and captions.
